open_findings.body:
[High] `evaluateCandidatesWithTimeout` — the new `await evaluation.catch(() => {});` in the `catch` block is unbounded, so `LOCAL_RUNTIME_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT_MS` is no longer an upper bound on the local phase and `LAMBDA_RESPONSE_HEADROOM_MS` is no longer guaranteed. (Anchoring note: the diff's hunk headers for this file are internally inconsistent, so no line number is given — the target is the `await evaluation.catch(() => {})` line inside the new `catch (error)` block of `evaluateCandidatesWithTimeout`.)

The abort only stops work at the cooperative `signal?.throwIfAborted()` checkpoints; anything already in flight has to finish on its own. The worst case is `await connectToDatabase()` (`api/utils/db.js`), which takes no signal, serialises on a module-level mutex, and connects with `serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 10000` — so it can hold for ~10s after the abort with nothing able to cancel it.

Worked example on the real config (`serverless.yml` `onboardingSearchGeneration`, `timeout: 30`, behind API Gateway's 29s cap): generation leaves ~12s, so `runtimeEvaluationBudgetMs = 12000 - 5000 = 7000` and the local timeout fires at t=5000. If a cold-start or failover `connectToDatabase()` is in flight, the settle wait runs to ~t=15000 — past the 12s that were left — and the Lambda hard-times-out with no body instead of returning a payload. Before this PR the `Promise.race` returned `runtime_evaluation_error` at exactly t=5000 with the full 5s headroom intact. Any deadline re-check before the Manhattan phase is too late: the overrun has already happened by the time control returns.

Suggest bounding the settle wait against the time actually left rather than awaiting it unconditionally — e.g. `await Promise.race([evaluation.catch(() => {}), delay(Math.max(0, runtimeEvaluationDeadline - Date.now()))])` — so the no-overlap guarantee never costs more than the remaining budget.
open_findings.failure_path: Lambda cold start or Mongo failover puts a non-abortable `connectToDatabase()` (serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 10000, behind a mutex) in flight inside `evaluateCandidates`. At t=5000ms the local timeout fires and aborts, but the new `await evaluation.catch(() => {})` blocks until that connect settles, up to t≈15000ms. With generation having already consumed ~18s of the 30s Lambda, only ~12s remained, so the handler is killed by the Lambda/API-Gateway timeout and the client gets a 504 with no body — where before the PR the race returned a graceful `runtime_evaluation_error` at t=5000ms with 7s to spare. The 5s `LAMBDA_RESPONSE_HEADROOM_MS` reservation that the unit test asserts is silently bypassed because the settle wait is outside the budget accounting.

open_findings.body:
[Medium] `query.setOptions({... signal})` here and the identical block in `api/model/googlePlaceTypes.js` look like they do nothing. `api/package.json` pins `mongoose@^7.8.3` (Node driver 5.x); as far as I can tell neither Mongoose 7's query options nor the driver's `FindOptions` understand an `AbortSignal` — unknown keys are dropped when the find command is built, so an abort mid-query will not cancel it. If that's right, the only real bound on these queries is `maxTimeMS`, and the "cancellation is threaded into the Mongo queries" guarantee that the new settle-wait in `evaluateCandidatesWithTimeout` leans on doesn't hold. Related: `api/businessLogic/smartSearch/smartSearchV3.js:530` passes `{signal}` but no `maxTimeMS`, so that call gets no bound at all.

I might be mistaken here — can you point at the mongoose/driver support for the option? Otherwise I'd drop `signal` from `setOptions`, keep `maxTimeMS`, and rely on the explicit `throwIfAborted()` checkpoints, so the code doesn't read as if the query is cancellable when it isn't.
open_findings.failure_path: Not a crash — a false guarantee. If mongoose 7 / driver 5 ignore the `signal` option, an aborted local evaluation keeps its in-flight `PlaceCategory.find` / `GooglePlaceType.find` running until the server-side `maxTimeMS` expires, so the settle wait added in this PR costs up to RUNTIME_DATABASE_MAX_TIME_MS per in-flight query instead of returning promptly. This is the mechanism behind f1 and it also makes the reply on the Baz thread ("cancellation is threaded into active-category and Google-place-type Mongo queries") inaccurate.

open_findings.body:
[Medium] All three rescue regressions use `geo: {lat: 0, lon: 0}`, and this PR also rewrites the pre-existing mission-preview test from `{lat: 41.3874, lon: 2.1686}` (Barcelona) to the same value. `0` is falsy in JS, so any `if (geo?.lat && geo?.lon)`-style guard on the selection path takes its no-usable-geo branch under these tests. The production scenario this PR is fixing is a user who *does* have a location and whose local coverage evaluation times out — with (0,0) the regressions may be proving a different branch than the one being repaired.

What made the geo change necessary? If it isn't load-bearing, please keep real coordinates so the new tests match the production path; if it is load-bearing, that coupling is worth a line in the test name.
open_findings.failure_path: No proven runtime failure — a test-validity concern. If any guard on the path treats falsy lat/lon as "no geo", the three new rescue tests exercise the degenerate-location branch rather than the timed-out-local-coverage branch, so the regression coverage the PR cites as proof would not actually pin the fixed behavior, and a future change to the real-geo path could regress silently.

open_findings.body:
Question on the approach, not a blocker. `const missionPreviewOnly = hasMissionPreview;` makes the preview-only shortcut apply to *every* Manhattan retry, not just the runtime-rescue one: `manhattanGenerationResult.searches` becomes `[manhattanPreviewSearch]` with `primary_search_index: 0` whenever a mission preview exists. The pre-existing insufficient-results retry used to evaluate all generated searches *plus* the appended preview in Manhattan, so a personalised generated query could still win there; after this PR that path can only ever return the generic mission preview. The updated test at the top of the file (4 searches -> 1) is that behavior change, not a rescue-path test.

Is narrowing the existing insufficient-results path intended as part of this fix, or should the preview-only shortcut be gated on `localEvaluationFailed` so the timeout rescue stays bounded without changing the non-rescue retry? (Anchoring note: no line number — the diff's hunk headers for this file are inconsistent; the target is the `const missionPreviewOnly = hasMissionPreview;` line in `evaluateAndSelectOnboardingHero`.)
open_findings.failure_path: No failure path — product/behavior question. Users on the existing insufficient-results retry lose the chance of a personalised query succeeding in Manhattan and always get the generic mission preview instead.

open_findings.body: Briefing only, do not post. Two process/verification gaps I could not close from the diff: (a) no Fibery task linked (`signals.fibery_linked = false`) — Aviad's standard steps-server holdup; (b) `manhattan_runtime_rescue` is a brand-new `reason_family` value and the local clone is at a ref that predates this whole module, so I could not check whether any dashboard, alert, or client consumer enumerates the allowed reason families. Worth a look before the telemetry is relied on for the 4.36.0 launch decision.
open_findings.failure_path: No failure path. Process gate plus an unverifiable telemetry-consumer question, recorded so it is not mistaken for something I checked.
